slot.brief: Solve a trigonometric equation combining sin and cos (reducible via t-formulas or auxiliary angle) and write the general solution.

stem: The general solution of $\sin x+\cos x=2\sin 2x$ is (where $\alpha=\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1+\sqrt{17}}{4\sqrt2}\right)$ and $\beta=\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1-\sqrt{17}}{4\sqrt2}\right)$)

verdicts.working: Set y=x+π/4. Then √2 sin y = -2 cos 2y, giving 2 sin²y − sin y/√2 − 1 = 0. Hence sin y = (1±√17)/(4√2). The two sine branches for each value yield option A.

working:
$u=\sin x+\cos x=\sqrt2\sin\left(x+\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$; $\sin2x=u^2-1$. $u=2(u^2-1)\Rightarrow 2u^2-u-2=0\Rightarrow u=\dfrac{1\pm\sqrt{17}}4$. Thus $\sin\left(x+\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)=\sin\alpha$ or $\sin\beta$; each gives $x=\theta-\dfrac{\pi}{4}+2n\pi$ or $x=\dfrac{3\pi}{4}-\theta+2n\pi$.

Independent check: Set y=x+π/4. Then √2 sin y = -2 cos 2y, giving 2 sin²y − sin y/√2 − 1 = 0. Hence sin y = (1±√17)/(4√2). The two sine branches for each value yield option A.
